I think the primary issues is that Doom 3 and Doom 4 (which I haven't played, so I'm just speculating here) may be decent first person shooters, but not particularly good Doom games if you judge them by the qualities of Doom I and II. I think this becomes especially apparent when you consider the speed of the two groups - Doom 1 and 2 were effectively arcade shooters where horror only played a minimal role (not that the scream of a revenant doesn't still lead to involuntary twitching in Doom Veterans).

Compared to that, Doom 3 was much akin to a horror shooter (i.e., based on its flashlight mechanic, amongst other things), which naturally came with a slower movement/playing speed. From what I have seen from trailers, Doomguy in Doom 4 also moves much slower than his precedessors - perhaps because the games' graphics have become increasingly important over the years, so you want the player to see as much of them as possible.
